claims.text: A sputter-deposited Hf interlayer approximately 50–100 nm thick should be placed between the Zr-alloy substrate and the elemental Cr coating.
The Hf interlayer will react with the Zr-alloy substrate.
Reaction of the Hf interlayer with the substrate will form an Hf–Zr intermetallic transition layer.
The resulting Hf–Zr transition layer will be chemically bonded and uniform.
The Hf–Zr intermetallic transition layer will remain stable under the proposed service and accident exposures.
The Hf–Zr intermetallic transition layer has low atomic diffusivity.
The Hf–Zr transition layer will act as a diffusion barrier to Cr and Zr atoms at elevated temperatures.
The Hf interlayer will markedly reduce formation and growth of the Cr–Zr interdiffusion zone relative to a Cr-coated Zr alloy without an interlayer.
Restricting Cr–Zr interdiffusion will preserve the integrity and adhesion of the elemental Cr coating.
The Hf interlayer will prevent premature Cr-coating failure under subcritical-water operation at approximately 320°C.
The Hf interlayer will prevent premature Cr-coating failure during steam exposure at approximately 900°C for 1 hour.
Approximately 320°C in subcritical water represents normal PWR operating conditions relevant to the coating.
Steam exposure at approximately 900°C for 1 hour represents an accident-relevant condition.
A Cr coating deposited directly on the Zr-alloy substrate suffers premature failure caused by Cr–Zr interdiffusion during high-temperature exposure.
Reducing the Cr–Zr interdiffusion zone will prolong protective performance in long-term PWR water.
Reducing the Cr–Zr interdiffusion zone will improve protective performance in short-term high-temperature steam.
